query: What should I do with my retirement savings to maintain steady income while keeping risk low?

recommendations.title: Increase Bond Allocation for Capital Preservation
recommendations.summary: Shift portfolio to 60% bonds to better align with conservative risk profile and income needs in retirement
recommendations.detailed_rationale: At age 65 with a loss comfort of only 2/10 and high liquidity needs, your current 50% bond allocation is slightly aggressive. Increasing to 60% bonds provides more stability and predictable income. With $1.2M in assets generating $78K annual income, preserving capital is paramount. The bond-heavy allocation reduces volatility while maintaining income generation through coupon payments. Consider maintaining your quality holdings in BND and AGG while reducing equity exposure from the 25% stock + 5% ETF (30% total) down to 25% total equities.
recommendations.suggested_action: Increase bond holdings by $120,000 (from $600K to $720K) by reducing stock positions proportionally

recommendations.title: Establish Monthly Income Distribution Strategy
recommendations.summary: Create systematic monthly distributions from dividend-paying holdings to supplement retirement income
recommendations.detailed_rationale: With monthly expenses of $4,200 ($50,400 annually) and income of $78,000, you have a comfortable surplus. However, optimizing cash flow is essential for retirement peace of mind. Your holdings in VYM, JNJ, PG, KO, DUK, SO, and VZ are excellent dividend payers. Set up automatic monthly distributions combining bond interest and stock dividends to generate approximately $3,000-3,500 monthly ($36K-42K annually, representing 3-3.5% yield). This provides regular income while leaving principal largely intact and maintaining your emergency fund in the 20% cash allocation.
recommendations.suggested_action: Establish automatic monthly distributions from dividend income; reinvest excess dividends

recommendations.title: Maintain Quality Dividend Aristocrats
recommendations.summary: Continue holding defensive blue-chip dividend payers that provide reliable income with minimal volatility
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your current equity holdings are exceptionally well-chosen for a conservative retiree. JNJ, PG, KO are Dividend Aristocrats with 25+ years of consecutive dividend increases. DUK and SO are regulated utilities providing steady 3.5-4.5% yields with low volatility. VZ offers high yield around 6-7%. These companies operate in defensive sectors (Healthcare 30%, Utilities 25%, Consumer Staples 20%) that perform well during economic uncertainty. Given your intermediate investment experience and conservative profile, these are ideal holdings. Do not sell these positions—they provide the stable, growing income stream you need.
recommendations.suggested_action: Hold all current dividend-paying stocks; consider adding to positions on market dips

recommendations.title: Reduce Cash Drag with Short-Term Treasury Ladder
recommendations.summary: Convert 10% of cash holdings to short-term Treasury ladder for higher yield while maintaining liquidity
recommendations.detailed_rationale: Your 20% cash allocation ($240,000) is appropriate for high liquidity needs and emergency fund requirements, but pure cash earns minimal return. With no debt and stable income, you can optimize $120,000 (10% of portfolio) by creating a 6-12 month Treasury ladder while keeping $120,000 in immediate cash access. Short-term Treasuries currently yield 4.5-5.0% versus near-zero in savings accounts, adding $5,000-6,000 annually in risk-free income. This maintains liquidity (Treasuries are highly liquid) while reducing opportunity cost. Keep remaining 10% in high-yield savings for true emergencies and monthly expenses.
recommendations.suggested_action: Move $120,000 from cash to 3-6-9-12 month Treasury ladder using TreasuryDirect
